claims.claim: Q4 revenue was $90.0 billion, up 18% year over year.
Q4 revenue was up 17% in constant currency.
Q4 operating income was $40.6 billion, up 18%.
Q4 net income was $35.8 billion, up 31% on a GAAP basis.
Q4 net income was $35.3 billion, up 22%, on a non-GAAP basis.
Q4 diluted EPS was $4.81, up 32%, on a GAAP basis.
Q4 diluted EPS was $4.74, up 23%, on a non-GAAP basis.
The non-GAAP measures exclude the impact from investments in OpenAI.
The impact from investments in OpenAI increased net income by $480 million and diluted EPS by $0.07 in the quarter.
Management states that discrete items produced a $0.27 diluted EPS benefit versus its April 29, 2026 guidance.
The discrete items include a $3.2 billion gain on Microsoft's Anthropic investment.
The discrete items include lower-than-expected Voluntary Retirement Program expenses, partly offset by severance and XBOX impairment charges.
Adjusting for the discrete items, the company says it exceeded expectations on revenue, operating income and diluted EPS.
Full-year FY2026 revenue was $331.8 billion, up 18% (up 16% in constant currency).
Full-year FY2026 operating income was $155.2 billion, up 21%.
Full-year FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS was $17.95, up 32%.
Full-year FY2026 non-GAAP diluted EPS increased 22%.
Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion, up 32% (up 31% in constant currency).
Intelligent Cloud segment operating income was $15,955 million versus $12,140 million a year earlier.
Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 43%.
Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion, up 27%.
Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $37.8 billion, up 14%.
Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 14% on a reported basis, or 16% adjusted for a prior-year comparable that benefited from 2 points of in-period revenue recognition.
LinkedIn revenue increased 12%.
Dynamics 365 revenue increased 13%.
More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion, down 4% (down 5% in constant currency).
More Personal Computing operating income was $2,748 million versus $3,190 million a year earlier.
Windows OEM and Devices revenue fell 7%.
XBOX content and services revenue fell 10%.
Search advertising revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs rose 10%.
Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 84% to $678 billion.
Management cites full-year Azure revenue surpassing $100 billion.
Management cites over 30 million Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats.
The release contains no guidance figures and states only that forward-looking guidance will be provided on the earnings conference call and webcast.
Q4 operating cash flow was $55,441 million.
Additions to property and equipment were $35,802 million in the quarter and $115,948 million for FY2026, versus $17,079 million and $64,551 million in the prior-year periods.
Cash, equivalents and short-term investments were $76,843 million at June 30, 2026, versus $94,565 million a year earlier.
Net property and equipment was $313,076 million versus $204,966 million a year earlier.
Microsoft returned $10.2 billion via dividends and share repurchases in Q4 FY2026.
Full-year PP&E additions of $115,948 million came against a declining cash and short-term investment balance.
Other income (expense), net swung to $3,444 million from $(1,707) million.
The OpenAI adjustment moved from a $1,575 million drag to a $480 million benefit year over year.
RPO was $678 billion, up 84%.
